insight.title: Why Faster Tools Make Your Workday Longer
insight.subtitle: Why saving time often results in having less of it

sections.text: Think about your inbox. It stays full because sending an email is now free and instant. When a task becomes easier to perform, we don't do less of it; we do more.

In 1865, William Jevons observed that as steam engines used coal more efficiently, total coal consumption actually skyrocketed. Increased efficiency lowers the "cost" of an action, which inevitably explodes the demand for it.
You make this mistake every time you adopt "faster" technology. You focus on the time saved per task, while ignoring that the tool’s ease of use will simply attract more tasks to do.
Try this today: When you use a time-saving shortcut today, decide exactly how you will spend the minutes saved.
Technology doesn’t clear your plate; it just makes the plate bigger.
